first_run: The first run passed 20 of 25 steps. One failure was a real bug (step 5, fixed above). The other four were mistakes in the test's own expectations, corrected before the final run: step 7 expected the versions list to count the current content too (it lists earlier versions only, which is right); step 12 looked for the word 'profile' while the page is titled 'Data quality report'; step 16 expected the wallet to drop by exactly 5.00, but the new IntraForge Pay paid 0.25 cashback back (the cashback feature working); step 25 looked for the sign-out button behind an account menu, while it is directly in the sidebar.
confirmed: Auto-publish under harmongt.uk: a new website was published as scenario-11081357.harmongt.uk with nobody pressing anything, and answered from the internet through Cloudflare (HTTP 200); switching auto-publish off took the name back (HTTP 404) and kept shop.harmongt.uk, which was published by hand.
IntraForge Pay cashback: a 5.00 payment paid 0.25 back into the customer's wallet.
Optimistic switches: an app's Disable/Enable reacts at once.
Smoother pages: page changes fade, dialogs ease in, new table rows fade in, and pages already seen open from memory.
not_covered: Uninstall: not run on this PC, because it removes things for the whole PC (start-up entry, backup tasks, shortcut, firewall rules) and would affect the real shop. It needs a spare PC or a virtual machine.
A real Windows restart, a second PC on the shop network, and the installer on a brand-new PC: need the hardware.
The Android wallet app on a real phone: needs Shop network switched on and a phone; the app's code was checked, not run on a device.

Paying an invoice by scanning the QR with a phone camera: the QR was shown (step 15); the payment itself was confirmed through the wallet's own interface (step 16) and, on 4 November, by decoding the QR from Spare Parts and the Pharmacy.
Real money: IntraForge Pay uses simulated IF Credits only.
